audit.whatIsWrong: Three decisive interactions were absent and one was misattributed. (a) Hookshot was described as 'her engage/stun' with no mention that it must grab a WALL to launch — the single most actionable fact in the matchup. (b) Tactical Sweep was described as a flat cone heal; Riot's text says only enemies in the OUTER half are slowed, take extra damage and heal her, so standing close is a free counterplay that was never stated. (c) Camille goes untargetable through The Hextech Ultimatum's dash, so a Depth Charge fired into it is a wasted 120s. (d) whys[1] calls Tactical Sweep the true-damage ability — the true damage is on Precision Protocol (Q).
audit.why: Every one of these changes what a player does with their hands. 'Fight away from walls' beats 'track her engage'; 'stand inside the cone' beats 'she heals'; 'do not fire R into her R' beats 'her ult isolates you'.
audit.corrected: Hookshot now carries its wall requirement and 16s rank-1 cooldown; Tactical Sweep's outer-half rule is stated in a Don't, in itemisation and in wants.foe[1]; the untargetable dash is written into spikes[3], whys[4] and mid; the true damage is moved to Precision Protocol.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four of seven chart rows contradicted their own whys. whys[3] says 'She owns the hard-commit window' under a 'Skill' token; whys[5] says 'Genuinely even' under 'Camille'; whys[6] says 'You reclaim relevance in teamfights' under 'Camille'; whys[0] has Nautilus favoured in auto-trades under 'Skill'.
audit.why: packet.levelChart is Nautilus/Camille/Camille/Camille/Skill/Skill/Nautilus, matching all seven whys, and the packet lists no defects for this matchup.
audit.corrected: Chart set to the packet order in BOTH layers as matched pairs, ratings raised on the two Nautilus rows.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 spike claimed Depth Charge 'beats her E hookshot escape' with no caveat, which reads as a green light to fire R into her all-in.
audit.why: It beats Hookshot, but not the R dash she is untargetable through. Those are two different windows and the page treated level 6 as one.
audit.corrected: Level 6 now separates the two: fire inside Hookshot's 16 seconds of downtime, never into The Hextech Ultimatum's dash.

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d were generic boilerplate that did not match their own titles ('Get E-stunned into her combo', 'Fight near walls').
audit.why: The combo opens on a Precision Protocol auto reset, and Hookshot's wall requirement is precisely why 'fight near walls' is a mistake — both titles had the right idea and no supporting text.
audit.corrected: Both Don'ts rewritten to state the actual mechanic behind their titles.

edits.before: Level 1 is roughly even — I have no all-in without W and E yet — but my passive Staggering Blow root makes auto-trades favor me, so punish her if she walks up to last-hit. The moment I hit level 3 with Q + W + E I own this lane: Dredge Line yanks her in, my passive roots her, and Titan's Wrath splash plus the burn wins the short trade while she's still kiting. The thing to respect is her E hookshot — if she stuns me into her Q-proc-and-W-cone combo my trade flips, so land my Q pull on MY terms, not when she's already dashing in. Bait her E first, then commit.
edits.after: Level 1 is roughly even — I have no all-in without W and E yet — but my passive Staggering Blow root makes auto-trades favor me, so punish her if she walks up to last-hit. The moment I hit level 3 with Q + W + E I own this lane: Dredge Line yanks her in, my passive roots her, and Titan's Wrath splash plus the burn wins the short trade while she's still kiting. The thing to respect is Hookshot — it has to grab a wall to launch and is down 16 seconds, so hold the middle of the lane and land my Q pull on MY terms. Bait her E first, then commit.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are where Camille's level-3 combo gets real — her Q true-damage stacks and W cone heal out-trade me in extended melee if she catches me, so I hold my Q pull as an engage-or-escape tool and don't throw it on cooldown. At 6 it evens out: Depth Charge is a long-range, undodgeable knock-up that beats her E escape, so if I land it while her hookshot is down I still win the all-in — but a fed Camille with E up and items starting can answer, so this is a genuine skill window, not a free kill. Use Riptide's slow to stick to her after the R lands and don't let her wall-dash out of the chain.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are where Camille's level-3 combo gets real — Precision Protocol's true damage and Tactical Sweep's outer-half heal out-trade me in extended melee, so I hold my Q pull as an engage-or-escape tool and don't throw it on cooldown. At 6 it evens out: Depth Charge is a long-range, undodgeable knock-up that beats her Hookshot escape, so landing it inside that 16 seconds still wins the all-in — but never fire it into her R dash, because she is untargetable through it and I lose 120 seconds for nothing. Use Riptide's slow to stick after the R lands, and keep the fight off the walls.

notes: Camille's Hookshot needing a wall, and Tactical Sweep healing only from its OUTER half, were both absent from the entire entry — those two are the highest-value additions here. Two derived flags I did NOT build advice on: Adaptive Defenses carries a 'percentHealth' flag, but Riot's text says the SHIELD is a percentage of Camille's own max health, not damage scaling off yours, so the existing 'Stack pure HP vs her W' framing has no support in the kit and I left that title alone (it is 22 characters and under the applier's threshold anyway); and The Hextech Ultimatum carries a 'channel' flag while Riot's description says only that she dashes and anchors the target — see questionsForUser.
